name: Herod Antipas
title: The Tetrarch Who Beheaded John
summary: Herod Antipas was the son of Herod the Great and ruled as tetrarch over Galilee and Perea. He is best known for beheading John the Baptist and for his role in the trial of Jesus, where he was sent to him by Pilate.

keyEvents.title: Imprisonment of John the Baptist
keyEvents.description: Herod Antipas imprisoned John the Baptist because John rebuked him for taking his brother's wife Herodias.

keyEvents.title: Beheading of John the Baptist
keyEvents.description: During a birthday party, Herod promised to give Salome whatever she asked for. At her mother's urging, she requested the head of John the Baptist on a platter.

keyEvents.title: Herod hears about Jesus
keyEvents.description: When Herod heard about Jesus and his miracles, he believed that John the Baptist had risen from the dead.

keyEvents.title: Herod wants to kill Jesus
keyEvents.description: Some Pharisees warned Jesus that Herod intended to kill him, but Jesus called Herod a fox and continued on his way.

keyEvents.title: Jesus is sent to Herod during the trial
keyEvents.description: Pilate sent Jesus to Herod when he learned that Jesus was from Galilee. Herod was glad to see Jesus and hoped to see a sign, but Jesus did not answer him.
